boring_rival_explanations: Undercoverage is driven by small calibration set size per stratum, not reactivity per se; high-reactivity subjects happen to fall in small strata.
The conformity score function (softmax margin) is globally miscalibrated for high-arousal states, not subject-specific.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: If calibration set size per stratum is doubled via data augmentation, undercoverage for high-reactivity subjects disappears entirely.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Undercoverage persists for high-reactivity subjects (>2 SD above stratum mean EDA peak) even when stratum calibration size is increased to >100 via bootstrap resampling, while low-reactivity subjects achieve nominal coverage at n=30.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Test by simulating increased calibration size via stratified bootstrap. If rival holds, coverage deficit should vanish with larger n; if mechanism holds, deficit remains due to distributional shift.

possible_confounders: Skin hair density at wrist site
Activity type during stress (speaking vs. mental arithmetic)
boring_rival_explanations: Motion artifacts affect all subjects equally during high-stress periods; the feature extractor is simply not robust to motion, not subject-specific.
Coverage drop is due to stressor intensity correlating with motion, not subject-specific coupling.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: All subjects show similar coverage degradation when test-period ACC magnitude exceeds a fixed threshold (e.g., >90th percentile of population baseline), regardless of individual coupling coefficients.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Coverage deficit correlates strongly with subject-specific motion-artifact coupling coefficient (slope of SQI on ACC during stress) but not with raw ACC magnitude alone; subjects with high ACC but low coupling maintain coverage.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Compute coupling coefficient per subject via mixed model: SQI ~ ACC + (1|subject) during stress. Stratify by coupling tertiles and test ACC-coverage relationship within each.

possible_confounders: Sliding window overlap percentage (induces artificial autocorrelation)
Inter-trial interval duration (shorter intervals → incomplete recovery)
Number of stress-rest cycles per subject
boring_rival_explanations: Observed dependence is entirely due to overlapping sliding windows; using non-overlapping windows eliminates the coverage deficit.
The effective sample size correction (n_eff) is unnecessary because Mondrian's exchangeability assumption holds for block-exchangeable sequences.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Switching to non-overlapping windows (step = window length) with inter-trial intervals >5×tau eliminates coverage deficit for all subjects, including slow recoverers.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Slow-recovery subjects (tau_EDA >60s) still show coverage deficit with non-overlapping windows and sufficient inter-trial intervals, while fast recoverers achieve nominal coverage; block bootstrap calibration restores coverage only for slow recoverers.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Recompute conformity scores with non-overlapping windows. Compare coverage before/after. Fit block bootstrap with block length = 2×tau. If mechanism holds, block bootstrap fixes coverage for slow recoverers only.

control_variables: Physiological arousal index (PC1 of EDA peak, HRV drop, HR increase)
Label bias score (VAS - predicted arousal, standardized)
boring_rival_explanations: Self-report labels are randomly noisy (classical measurement error), not systematically biased; undercoverage stems from classifier error on noisy labels.
Under-reporters have genuinely lower physiological arousal; the 'bias' reflects true inter-subject variability in stress response.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Relabeling calibration samples using a physiological arousal threshold (e.g., top 30% of arousal index = 'stress') does not improve coverage for under-reporters compared to using original labels.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Coverage for strong under-reporters (label bias < -1 SD) increases by >15 percentage points after physiological relabeling, while coverage for accurate reporters (|bias| < 0.5 SD) changes by <3 points.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: WESAD has VAS after each condition. Compute arousal index from EDA/HRV/HR during stress. Define physiological label: arousal >75th percentile = stress. Retrain/calibrate with new labels and compare coverage per bias group.

control_variables: Physiological phenotype cluster (k-means on baseline features)
boring_rival_explanations: Phenotype extremes are simply outliers with poor model fit; removing them yields nominal coverage for remaining subjects.
Continuous phenotypes are redundant with demographic strata; adding them does not improve exchangeability.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Data-driven physiological clustering (k-means on baseline HRV, BRS, HR) yields strata with equivalent coverage to demographic stratification; no reduction in coverage deficit for phenotype extremes.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Physiological clustering reduces coverage deficit for subjects >2 SD from demographic stratum centroid on baseline HRV by >50% compared to demographic strata, while maintaining coverage for central subjects.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Compute baseline HRV/BRS from WESAD rest period. Assign demographic strata (age median split × sex). Compute coverage per HRV quantile within strata. Test k-means (k=4-6) on [HRV, BRS, HR] for alternative strata. Compare coverage distributions.

control_variables: SCL drift rate (µS/min, linear slope over recording)
Mean ACC during recording (proxy for movement-induced electrode shift)
boring_rival_explanations: SCL drift is random and non-systematic; conformity score drift is due to physiological adaptation, not sensor degradation.
All subjects experience similar drift; coverage decreases uniformly over time, not selectively for high-sweat subjects.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Detrending conformity scores (subtracting linear time trend) does not improve coverage for high baseline SCL subjects; early vs. late coverage gap persists.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Subjects with baseline SCL >0.5 µS show >10% coverage drop from early (first 30%) to late (last 30%) test windows; detrending conformity scores restores late-window coverage to within 3% of early-window coverage for these subjects, while low-SCL subjects show <2% change.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: WESAD EDA at 4 Hz. Compute SCL per 1-min window, fit linear drift. Split test windows early/late. Fit conformity score ~ time per subject. Test coverage before/after subtracting subject-specific time trend.

possible_confounders: Medication affecting cardiovascular physiology (beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers)
Feature extraction pipeline differences (e.g., HRV time vs. frequency domain)
Classifier training set composition (class balance, subject overlap)
control_variables: Feature space density (mean 5-NN distance in training feature space)
Subject-level Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on calibration set
Conformity score type (softmax margin vs. temperature-scaled)
boring_rival_explanations: The classifier is globally miscalibrated (high ECE for all subjects); out-of-distribution subjects are not uniquely affected.
Low feature density subjects have higher coverage because they are 'easier' to classify (distinctive patterns), not harder.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Temperature scaling (learned on calibration set) eliminates coverage deficit uniformly across all feature density quantiles.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Temperature scaling reduces coverage deficit to <2% for low-density subjects (feature density <5th percentile) but has minimal effect (<1% change) for high-density subjects; raw softmax margin shows >15% deficit for low-density vs. <3% for high-density.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Extract WESAD stress classifier features. Compute 5-NN density in training feature space. Estimate per-subject ECE on calibration. Apply temperature scaling (single T learned on calibration). Compare coverage per density bin.

possible_confounders: Sleep duration and quality prior to recording
control_variables: Hours from habitual wake time (estimated from sleep diary or actigraphy)
boring_rival_explanations: Time-of-day effects are due to fatigue accumulation (hours awake), not circadian biology; coverage declines monotonically with time awake.
Morning vs. afternoon differences reflect stressor order effects (TSST always first/last), not circadian phase.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Coverage varies linearly with hours since waking (fatigue), not sinusoidally with circadian phase; adding 'hours awake' as a stratification covariate eliminates the time-of-day coverage pattern.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Coverage shows a significant sinusoidal component (p<0.05, cosinor analysis) with nadir at ~16:00 (cortisol trough) after controlling for hours awake; adding circadian phase (estimated from temperature minimum) as a stratum covariate improves coverage more than adding hours awake.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: WESAD timestamps give recording start. Estimate habitual wake at 7 AM. Compute hours awake at stressor. Fit cosinor model: coverage ~ cos(2π*t/24) + sin(2π*t/24) + hours_awake. Test significance of circadian terms.

possible_confounders: Stratum definition granularity (age bins, sex only vs. adding BMI)
Calibration set composition (proportion of stress vs. non-stress)
Feature space dimensionality (curse of dimensionality in small strata)
Dependence within calibration set (violates i.i.d. assumption)
Outlier subjects in small strata distorting quantile estimation
control_variables: Physiological distinctiveness (Mahalanobis distance to stratum centroid)
Effective calibration size (n_eff from H3 autocorrelation correction)
boring_rival_explanations: Undercoverage in small strata is due to high physiological distinctiveness of subjects in those strata, not stratum size per se; large strata with distinctive subjects show same deficit.
The 1/(n+1) discretization is negligible; the real issue is that small strata have higher variance in conformity score distribution estimation.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Pooling small strata (n<30) with the nearest larger stratum (by centroid distance) does not improve coverage for distinctive subjects; coverage deficit is driven by distinctiveness, not n.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: For subjects with distinctiveness >2 SD in strata with n<20, pooling with nearest stratum (n>50) raises empirical coverage from <80% to >88% (nominal 90%), while distinctive subjects in large strata (n>50) already have >88% coverage without pooling.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Compute stratum sizes from WESAD demographic splits. Calculate Mahalanobis distance using calibration feature covariance. Simulate pooling: merge strata with n<20 to nearest stratum by centroid distance. Bootstrap coverage (1000 reps) for distinctive subjects pre/post pooling.

control_variables: Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ) reappraisal/suppression scores (if available)
Autonomic pathway index (cardiac: HR/HRV vs. vascular: EDA/SCL ratio during stress)
Physiological mode assignment (GMM cluster on stress features)
boring_rival_explanations: Physiological heterogeneity within 'stress' label is random noise; clustering finds spurious modes that do not replicate.
Different physiological patterns reflect different stressor intensities, not coping strategies; TSST elicits vascular-dominant, fun stressor elicits cardiac-dominant.
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Gaussian mixture modeling on stress-period physiological features yields a single component (BIC favors k=1); coverage deficit is unrelated to cluster membership.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: GMM on stress features (EDA peak, HRV drop, HR increase, SCL) selects k=2 components (BIC) with silhouette >0.5; subjects in the minority mode (n<30% of stratum) show >15% coverage deficit vs. majority mode; mode membership predicts ERQ suppression score (r>0.4) if ERQ available, or predicts coverage deficit in held-out data.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: WESAD lacks ERQ. Use physiological clustering as proxy: fit GMM on stress-window features (standardized). Test if mode membership predicts coverage deficit. If ERQ available in future data, test correlation. Stressor type (TSST vs. fun) must be controlled.
